question.problem: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does $\sqrt{40}$ lie?
question.worked_solution:
To find which two consecutive whole numbers $\sqrt{40}$ lies between, we first identify the perfect squares that are just below and just above $40.$

The perfect squares closest to $40$ are $36$ and $49.$ We have

$$
36<40<49.
$$

Taking the square root of each number, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{36} & <\sqrt{40}<\sqrt{49} \\ 6 & <\sqrt{40}<7.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14185481/assets/5c2775762ff274451dfd3258bacbede7240e6bad25b782cc86a76484e61d31bb.png)

Therefore, $\sqrt{40}$ lies between $6$ and $7.$
